title: 10 Years Language Learning: Lessons I'd Give My Younger Self
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: the ability to continue doing something regularly over a long period of time.
the process of surrounding yourself with a language so that you use and hear it constantly.
a high level of skill or ability in something, especially in a language.
a period when progress stops or becomes very slow after earlier improvement.
the reason or desire that makes someone do something.
the responsibility to complete tasks or achieve goals, often because someone else is checking your progress.
organized according to a clear plan or system.

sentences.en: In August 2016, I moved to a small town on the Japanese island of Shikoku.
sentences.zh: 2016年8月，我搬到了日本四国岛的一个小镇。

sentences.en: I had almost no Japanese ability and I didn’t have an expectation that I’d stay very long in Japan.
sentences.zh: 我几乎完全不会日语，而且当时也没指望在日本待太久。

sentences.en: Maybe I’d stay in Japan for one year. 10 years later, though, I’m still in Japan.
sentences.zh: 也许我会在日本待一年。然而10年过去了，我依然在日本。

sentences.en: I’m now married. I have a daughter. I run a business from Japan.
sentences.zh: 我现在结婚了，有个女儿，在日本经营着一家公司。

sentences.en: And I can live my entire life in Japanese if I need to.
sentences.zh: 如果需要的话，我可以用日语过上完全正常的生活。

sentences.en: Looking back, there are things that I’m incredibly proud of in my Japanese learning journey and a few things that I wish I had done differently.
sentences.zh: 回首过去，在我的日语学习之旅中，有些事让我感到无比骄傲，也有一些事让我希望能换种方式去做。

sentences.en: So in today’s episode of Thinking in English, I thought it would be interesting to discuss my past 10 years of language learning experiences: how I went from zero knowledge of Japanese to being able to live in Japanese daily if I need to.
sentences.zh: 所以在今天这期《Thinking in English》节目中，我觉得聊聊过去10年的语言学习经历会很有意思：我是如何从对日语一窍不通，到如今在需要时能够全日语日常生活的。

sentences.en: Hopefully by listening to this episode, you guys will receive some motivation and some advice about your own language learning journeys.
sentences.zh: 希望通过收听这期节目，你们能为自己的语言学习之旅获得一些动力和建议。

sentences.en: As I said at the beginning of this episode, I moved to Japan for the first time 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 正如我在节目开头所说，我第一次搬到日本是在10年前。

sentences.en: I moved to the island of Shikoku to be an Assistant Language Teacher after I graduated from university.
sentences.zh: 大学毕业后，我搬到了四国岛当一名外籍英语教师（ALT）。

sentences.en: In fact, it was my first job, and I had my 21st birthday in Japan.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是我的第一份工作，我的21岁生日也是在日本度过的。

sentences.en: I had absolutely no Japanese ability when I first moved to Japan.
sentences.zh: 刚搬到日本时，我完全不会日语。

sentences.en: Maybe I had spent a few weeks learning a few Japanese letters.
sentences.zh: 也许我花了几周时间学过几个日语假名。

sentences.en: I’d also been given one Japanese class to help me practice my Japanese self-introduction so that I could introduce myself to my new colleagues and other teachers at the schools I would be working at.
sentences.zh: 我还上过一节日语课，帮我练习日语自我介绍，这样我就能在即将工作的学校里向新同事和其他老师介绍自己了。

sentences.en: But I could not speak Japanese. I did not grow up interested in Japanese culture.
sentences.zh: 但我不会说日语。我从小对日本文化并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: I did not grow up watching Japanese TV or reading Japanese comic books.
sentences.zh: 我从小不看日本电视节目，也不读日本漫画书。

sentences.en: I did not grow up eating Japanese food. I knew nothing about Japan.
sentences.zh: 我从小不吃日本料理。我对日本一无所知。

sentences.en: You can find out more about why I moved to Japan in some previous Thinking in English episodes.
sentences.zh: 你可以在之前的一些《Thinking in English》节目中了解更多关于我为什么搬到日本的原因。

sentences.en: I think I did one last year about what I’ve learned from living abroad.
sentences.zh: 我想我去年做过一期关于海外生活感悟的节目。

sentences.en: But this episode, I want to be a bit more focused on my language learning journey.
sentences.zh: 但在这期节目中，我想更专注地聊聊我的语言学习历程。

sentences.en: 10 years ago, I spoke absolutely no Japanese.
sentences.zh: 10年前，我一句日语都不会说。

sentences.en: Today, I use Japanese every single day in my life.
sentences.zh: 如今，我的生活中每天都在使用日语。

sentences.en: I speak to my family in Japanese, my friends in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 我和家人说日语，和朋友说日语。

sentences.en: I use Japanese for my business paperwork, for when I go to the shop.
sentences.zh: 我的公司公文要用日语，去商店买东西也用日语。

sentences.en: I use the language every day. I’m still not at the level I would like to be, but I am fully communicative.
sentences.zh: 我每天都在使用这门语言。虽然我的水平还没达到自己期望的高度，但我已经能完全无障碍交流了。

sentences.en: I can speak in Japanese as much as I want to.
sentences.zh: 只要我想，我可以用日语畅所欲言。

sentences.en: So today, I want to talk about how the journey has happened.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我想谈谈这段旅程是如何展开的。

sentences.en: How I have gone from zero to my current level over the 10 years.
sentences.zh: 这10年里，我是如何从零基础走到今天的水平的。

sentences.en: And I want to do this to show you that progress is not necessarily a straight line.
sentences.zh: 我想借此告诉大家，进步未必是一条直线。

sentences.en: It’s also not always going to increase at the level you hope.
sentences.zh: 它也不总是会按照你期望的水平持续增长。

sentences.en: In my case, my first two years of studying Japanese were incredible.
sentences.zh: 就我而言，我学习日语的前两年简直不可思议。

sentences.en: I really, really, really improved quickly.
sentences.zh: 我的进步真的、真的、真的非常快。

sentences.en: And then the past eight years have been a bit more stagnant, a bit more of a plateau.
sentences.zh: 但在过去的八年里，情况变得有些停滞不前，进入了一个平台期。

sentences.en: I have improved, but just not as quickly as I did in those first two years.
sentences.zh: 我确实在进步，只是不像前两年那样迅速了。

sentences.en: That’s just the reality of trying to learn a language while working full-time.
sentences.zh: 这就是一边全职工作一边学语言的现实情况。

sentences.en: The way I’m going to structure this episode is to talk about five things that I’m proud of and then five things that I regret.
sentences.zh: 这期节目的结构是这样的：先聊聊让我感到骄傲的五件事，然后聊聊让我感到后悔的五件事。

sentences.en: So the first thing that I am proud of in my learning journey is that I never gave up.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我的学习之旅中，我感到骄傲的第一件事就是我从未放弃。

sentences.en: I never gave up studying. I have been studying Japanese continuously, maybe not as consistently as I want to, but I have been studying without giving up for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 我从未放弃学习。我一直在持续学习日语，也许不像我希望的那样规律，但我10年来从未放弃过学习。

sentences.en: This is probably the reason why my Japanese is still at a decent level.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是我的日语至今仍保持在不错水平的原因。

sentences.en: I know people who have lived in Japan for many years, and I know people who are married to Japanese people, but just never committed to language learning.
sentences.zh: 我认识一些在日本住了很多年的人，也认识一些娶了或嫁给日本人的人，但他们就是从不上心去学语言。

sentences.en: They cannot use Japanese professionally and really, they can’t use it personally either.
sentences.zh: 他们无法在职场上使用日语，说实话，私底下也无法使用。

sentences.en: In fact, last year I was asked to translate for someone who had lived in this town for the past 20 years but had never bothered to learn Japanese to a higher level.
sentences.zh: 事实上，去年有人请我帮忙给一个人做翻译，那人在这个小镇已经住了20年，却从来懒得把日语学到更高的水平。

sentences.en: So they asked me, a volunteer, to come in and help translate some kind of educational session.
sentences.zh: 所以他们找了我这个志愿者来帮忙翻译某种教育培训会议。

sentences.en: Something to bear in mind here is that, yes, I never gave up in my learning journey, but that does not mean that I have been studying at the same intensity over that period of time.
sentences.zh: 这里需要记住的一点是，是的，我的学习之旅从未中断，但这并不意味着我在整个时期都保持着相同的学习强度。

sentences.en: My motivation for studying has changed significantly over the past 10 years.
sentences.zh: 在过去的10年里，我学习的动力发生了很大变化。

sentences.en: When I started, my motivation to learn Japanese was survival.
sentences.zh: 刚开始的时候，我学日语的动力是为了生存。

sentences.en: I was working in a school with no English speakers.
sentences.zh: 我在一所没有英语使用者的学校工作。

sentences.en: I was living in a town with no friends, and I really just needed to speak some Japanese so that my life would be easier.
sentences.zh: 我住在一个没有朋友的小镇里，我真的需要说点日语，好让生活过得更容易些。

sentences.en: Then it became a hobby. I was interested in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 后来它变成了一种爱好。我对日语产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: I wanted to learn more. My motivation was enjoyment.
sentences.zh: 我想学更多。我的动力是享受其中。

sentences.en: This meant that I studied a bit less intensively.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我的学习强度有所下降。

sentences.en: When you need to study something, you tend to study harder than if you just like studying.
sentences.zh: 当你不得不学某种东西时，你往往会比单纯喜欢学习时学得更拼。

sentences.en: Then I studied Japanese as part of an educational requirement when I was a research student, so I took formal classes.
sentences.zh: 后来，当我作为研究生时，学日语成了学业要求的一部分，于是我开始上正规的课程。

sentences.en: And now I study Japanese both for enjoyment, but also to make sure that my family in the future, my wife and my daughter, we are a fully bilingual family.
sentences.zh: 现在我学日语既是为了兴趣，也是为了确保我们未来的家庭——我的妻子和女儿——能成为一个完全的双语家庭。

sentences.en: So that I am fluent in Japanese and that my wife is fluent in English, and that our child will be fluent in both languages as well.
sentences.zh: 好让我能说一口流利的日语，我的妻子能说一口流利的英语，我们的孩子也能精通这两种语言。

sentences.en: Sometimes I have studied really intensively over this past 10-year period.
sentences.zh: 在过去的10年里，有时我学习强度非常大。

sentences.en: Sometimes my progress really slowed down.
sentences.zh: 有时我的进度确实放缓了。

sentences.en: But I never stopped studying completely.
sentences.zh: 但我从未完全停止学习。

sentences.en: Even now, I’m not studying too much in my personal life, but every Friday morning, I take a Japanese class.
sentences.zh: 即使现在，我在个人生活中其实学得不多，但每周五早上，我都会上一堂日语课。

sentences.en: It’s that consistency over 10 years that really matters.
sentences.zh: 正是这10年如一日的坚持才真正重要。

sentences.en: The second thing I am proud of is going from zero to intermediate level in Japanese in one year.
sentences.zh: 我感到骄傲的第二件事，是在一年内从零基础达到了日语中级水平。

sentences.en: I started at an absolute beginner level.
sentences.zh: 我从绝对的零基础开始学起。

sentences.en: I did not know any Japanese vocabulary at all.
sentences.zh: 我完全不认识任何日语词汇。

sentences.en: I did not know any Japanese grammar. I did not know Japanese phonics.
sentences.zh: 我不懂任何日语语法。我也不懂日语发音。

sentences.en: I had no knowledge of the language at all.
sentences.zh: 我对这门语言一无所知。

sentences.en: I started to attend local Japanese community classes when I first moved to Japan.
sentences.zh: 刚搬到日本时，我开始参加当地的日本社区课程。

sentences.en: Most of my classmates were people working in more manual industries.
sentences.zh: 我的大部分同学都是从事偏体力劳动行业的人。

sentences.en: People working in shipbuilding or ship cleaning or in caregiving.
sentences.zh: 有从事造船、船舶清洁或护理工作的人。

sentences.en: Initially, I took two group classes a week, and then I added a third class, a private class as well, with one of my Japanese teachers.
sentences.zh: 起后来，我一周上两个集体班，后来又加了第三个班，也就是和其中一位日语老师上私教课。

sentences.en: I also studied personally myself every single day.
sentences.zh: 我每天也都进行个人自学。

sentences.en: I used to finish work, and then on the way home from work, I would stop in at a cafe or a restaurant and study for one hour.
sentences.zh: 我过去常常下班后，在下班回家的路上顺便去咖啡馆或餐厅学习一个小时。

sentences.en: I was fortunate because maybe I had a bit more time, personal time to study than my other classmates.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运，因为比起其他同学，我可能有更多的个人时间用来学习。

sentences.en: Within six months, I was the top of the class, and then I moved to the next level up in the classes.
sentences.zh: 在六个月内，我成了班里的第一名，然后我升入了更高阶的班级。

sentences.en: I passed the Japanese Language Proficiency Test N4 level, so that’s the second level of the test in my first eight months of studying Japanese.
sentences.zh: 在我学习日语的前八个月里，我通过了日语能力测试（JLPT）N4级别，也就是该考试的第二个级别。

sentences.en: And then one year later, I passed N3, which is intermediate Japanese.
sentences.zh: 一年后，我通过了N3，也就是日语中级。

sentences.en: Beginner learners can often underestimate how much progress is possible in a single year.
sentences.zh: 初学者往往会低估在短短一年内能取得多大的进步。

sentences.en: I went from nothing to having conversations in Japanese, and that is something I’m really proud of.
sentences.zh: 我从一无所知到能够用日语进行对话，这让我感到非常骄傲。

sentences.en: I have friends who moved to Japan the same time as me and never learned anything.
sentences.zh: 我有些朋友和我同时搬到日本，却什么都没学到。

sentences.en: I was not going to let that happen to me.
sentences.zh: 我可绝不让这种事发生在我身上。

sentences.en: I wanted to make progress. The third thing I am proud of is passing proficiency tests.
sentences.zh: 我想取得进步。我感到骄傲的第三件事是通过了能力测试。

sentences.en: The main proficiency test for Japanese, the equivalent of the IELTS exam or the TOEFL exam in Japanese, is the JLPT, the Japanese Language Proficiency Test.
sentences.zh: 日语的主要能力测试，相当于英语里的雅思或托福考试，就是JLPT（日语能力测试）。

sentences.en: And I have passed this test now three times.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，我已经三次通过了这个考试。

sentences.en: I passed the N4 level in 2017. I passed the N3 level in 2018.
sentences.zh: 我在2017年通过了N4级。我在2018年通过了N3级。

sentences.en: And I passed the N2 level recently, in the past two years.
sentences.zh: 最近两年内，我又通过了N2级。

sentences.en: And I’m really proud of these achievements.
sentences.zh: 我为这些成就感到由衷的骄傲。

sentences.en: The certification itself doesn’t really matter too much to me.
sentences.zh: 证书本身对我来说其实并不算太重要。

sentences.en: I don’t necessarily need it right now in my life.
sentences.zh: 目前我的生活中不一定非要用到它。

sentences.en: But what matters here is that passing these tests represents years of effort in my life.
sentences.zh: 但这里重要的是，通过这些考试代表了我生活中数年如一日的努力。

sentences.en: It is proof that my effort was worthwhile.
sentences.zh: 这是证明我的付出是值得的证据。

sentences.en: The fact I could pass tests is evidence that my Japanese was improving.
sentences.zh: 我能通过考试这一事实，证明了我的日语在不断提高。

sentences.en: I’ve also failed the exams. I failed the N2 exam my first time taking it back in 2021, and I also failed the N1 exam last year.
sentences.zh: 我也考砸过。早在2021年我第一次考N2时就挂了，去年考N1也失败了。

sentences.en: N1 is the highest level of Japanese proficiency test.
sentences.zh: N1是日语能力测试的最高级别。

sentences.en: Hopefully, in the future, I’m going to pass the N1 exam, but it’s not guaranteed.
sentences.zh: 希望在未来，我能通过N1考试，但这并不是百分之百保证的。

sentences.en: But I’m still proud of my effort. I’m proud of passing these exams.
sentences.zh: 但我依然为自己的努力感到骄傲。我为通过这些考试感到骄傲。

sentences.en: The fourth thing I am proud of in my Japanese learning journey is building real relationships in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 在我的日语学习之旅中，我感到骄傲的第四件事是用日语建立了真实的人际关系。

sentences.en: This is probably more important than my proficiency test results.
sentences.zh: 这可能比我的能力测试成绩还要重要。

sentences.en: My first attempts at making friends in Japanese were unsuccessful.
sentences.zh: 我最初尝试用日语交朋友并没有成功。

sentences.en: My Japanese level was not high enough. This was back 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我的日语水平还不够高。那是10年前的事了。

sentences.en: But when I moved to Tokyo during the COVID pandemic, I didn’t have many friends.
sentences.zh: 但在新冠疫情封城期间我搬到了东京，当时我没有多少朋友。

sentences.en: It was COVID. There too many international students moving to Japan.
sentences.zh: 那是疫情期间。没有太多国际学生搬到日本。

sentences.en: I was lucky that I was allowed to move to the country.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运自己获准入境。

sentences.en: And I started to go to this cafe maybe two or three times a week.
sentences.zh: 我开始一周去大概两三次咖啡馆。

sentences.en: I’d drink a nice cup of coffee, and gradually I started talking to the owner, and then I started talking to other regular customers.
sentences.zh: 我喝着一杯好咖啡，渐渐地开始跟老板聊天，然后开始跟其他常客聊天。

sentences.en: And in the end, I would visit this cafe all the time, and I would have amazing conversations.
sentences.zh: 最后，我总是去这家咖啡馆，并能进行非常精彩的对话。

sentences.en: The cafe also turned into a bar, so at nights I would go and meet more people and chat with people, and it was all 100% exclusively in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 这家咖啡馆后来也变成了一家酒吧，所以晚上我会去结识更多人并和大家聊天，而且全程100%只用日语。

sentences.en: It made me feel so happy, so proud that I was able to communicate with this variety of people who just five years before I would not have been able to talk to.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到非常高兴，也非常骄傲，因为我能够与形形色色的人交流，而就在五年前，我还根本无法与他们对话。

sentences.en: I’ve also built relationships with my wife’s family.
sentences.zh: 我也和妻子的一家人建立了联系。

sentences.en: I get on really well with my mother-in-law, my father-in-law, and my sister-in-law, and my brother-in-law, and all of that is done exclusively in Japanese as well.
sentences.zh: 我和岳母、岳父、小姨子、小叔子都相处得很好，而且所有这些交流也完全是用日语进行的。

sentences.en: I also try to participate in community life here in Japan.
sentences.zh: 我也努力融入日本当地的社区生活。

sentences.en: I try to attend events and volunteer in different things when I can.
sentences.zh: 只要有机会，我就会尽量参加各种活动并去做志愿者。

sentences.en: These conversations that I have now would have been impossible 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 如果是在10年前，我现在的这些对话是根本不可能实现的。

sentences.en: I have met people who I would never have been able to communicate with 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我遇到了一些人，如果放在10年前，我是绝对无法与他们沟通的。

sentences.en: So building relationships has been something I’m really proud of.
sentences.zh: 所以建立人际关系是我感到非常骄傲的一件事。

sentences.en: And the fifth thing I am proud of in my Japanese learning journey is public speaking.
sentences.zh: 在我的日语学习之旅中，我感到骄傲的第五件事是当众演讲。

sentences.en: I have been public speaking in Japanese since the first year I started studying.
sentences.zh: 从我开始学习的第一年起，我就一直在用日语进行公众演讲。

sentences.en: I have entered speech contests, I have given presentations, I have talked in front of people, and it is really fulfilling.
sentences.zh: 我参加过演讲比赛，做过展示，在众人面前发表过讲话，这真的很有成就感。

sentences.en: My first speech contest attempt was in 2017, within the first year of me studying Japanese.
sentences.zh: 我第一次尝试演讲比赛是在2017年，那是我学习日语的第一年。

sentences.en: I stood in front of an audience of people and talked about the English holiday of Pancake Day, which takes place on Shrove Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 我站在观众面前，讲述了英国的“煎饼日”这个节日，它是在忏悔星期二举行。

sentences.en: I had spent weeks practicing my speech. My Japanese teacher had helped me write a text, and I stood in front of people.
sentences.zh: 我花了好几个星期练习演讲。我的日语老师帮我写了稿子，然后我站在了大家面前。

sentences.en: I gave my speech. I was on TV. They featured me on the local news.
sentences.zh: 我发表了演讲。我还上了电视。当地新闻对我进行了报道。

sentences.en: And I won the beginner or the lower intermediate category in the speech contest.
sentences.zh: 我在演讲比赛中获得了初级或中初级组的冠军。

sentences.en: I was so proud of that achievement. The fact I had written something, practiced something, delivered it in public in front of an audience of people, all in Japanese, was such an amazing achievement.
sentences.zh: 我为这个成就感到无比骄傲。我写好了内容，练习过，并且在观众面前公开用日语把它表达出来，这真是一项了不起的成就。

sentences.en: The following year, I tried to do the same, but this time I entered the upper intermediate level of the speech contest.
sentences.zh: 第二年，我试图再次挑战，但这次我参加的是演讲比赛的中高级组。

sentences.en: And in front of an audience of people, I completely forgot my words.
sentences.zh: 结果在观众面前，我把词全忘光了。

sentences.en: I had made a much more challenging speech, a longer speech.
sentences.zh: 我准备了一篇更具挑战性、更长的演讲稿。

sentences.en: It was harder for me to remember. It was probably at the edge of my ability, and I forgot my words.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说更难记住。它可能已经达到了我能力边缘，结果我忘词了。

sentences.en: It was a bigger stage. There were more people watching me.
sentences.zh: 那是个更大的舞台。有更多的人在看着我。

sentences.en: I started to sweat, and I forgot everything that was happening.
sentences.zh: 我开始冒汗，脑子里发生的一切全都忘光了。

sentences.en: But instead of stopping me from speaking in public, it just encouraged me to keep going and keep trying.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有阻止我继续在公众面前讲话，反而激励着我继续前行、继续尝试。

sentences.en: I took a public speaking course when I was a student in Tokyo, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如，当我在东京做学生时，我还上过一门公众演讲课。

sentences.en: That was one of my favorite Japanese classes I’ve ever taken, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那是我上过的最喜欢的日语课之一。

sentences.en: It was a 10-week course on public speaking.
sentences.zh: 那是一个为期10周的公众演讲课程。

sentences.en: And in fact, it’s something I want to do for Thinking in English in the future.
sentences.zh: 其实，这也是我未来想为《Thinking in English》做的一件事。

sentences.en: And then last year, I entered another speech contest, speaking about the history of the region I currently live in.
sentences.zh: 去年，我又参加了一场演讲比赛，主题是我目前居住的地区的历史。

sentences.en: So I just really enjoy speaking in public.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很享受当众演讲。

sentences.en: Now, I get nervous, really nervous. But after every time I speak publicly, I feel proud of myself.
sentences.zh: 现在，我还是会紧张，真的很紧张。但每次公开演讲之后，我都为自己感到骄傲。

sentences.en: I prove that I can stand in front of an audience.
sentences.zh: 我证明了自己能够站在观众面前。

sentences.en: I prove that I can deliver a speech and handle the pressure.
sentences.zh: 我证明了自己能够发表演讲并顶住压力。

sentences.en: And I prove that I can express myself publicly.
sentences.zh: 我证明了自己能够在公众面前表达自我。

sentences.en: There are not many people who are confident enough to speak in a foreign language, and there are far fewer who are confident enough to stand in front of an audience and deliver a speech.
sentences.zh: 没有多少人有足够的自信去用外语演讲，而有足够的自信站在观众面前发表演讲的人就更少了。

sentences.en: Let’s move on to some things that I regret or things that I have learned along the way of my studying journey.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们转来聊聊我所后悔的一些事，或者是我在学习之路上学到的教训。

sentences.en: The first thing is that I assumed my progress would be linear.
sentences.zh: 第一件事是，我曾以为我的进步会是线性的。

sentences.en: Linear means a straight line. When I first started studying Japanese, those first two years, 2016 to 2018, I improved really quickly.
sentences.zh: 线性意味着一条直线。刚开始学日语的那前两年，也就是2016年到2018年，我的进步非常快。

sentences.en: I was going through a chapter of the textbook every week, learning new grammar points and new words every single day.
sentences.zh: 我基本上每周学完教科书的一个章节，每天都在学习新的语法点和新词汇。

sentences.en: My level was increasing rapidly. I assumed that if I kept studying as hard as I had been studying, if I kept my motivation and my consistency, my progress would be linear.
sentences.zh: 我的水平在迅速提升。我以为只要我一直像以前那样努力学习，保持动力和坚持，我的进步就会是线性的。

sentences.en: I would continue making progress. I went from beginner to intermediate.
sentences.zh: 我会继续取得进展。我从初学者跨越到了中级。

sentences.en: I would go from intermediate to advanced in the same time.
sentences.zh: 我本以为能在同样的时间内从初级跨入高级。

sentences.en: That is not what happened. I assume most of you guys have experienced similar things in the past.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。我想你们大多数人在过去也经历过类似的事情。

sentences.en: I assumed progress would be linear, a straight line.
sentences.zh: 我以为进步会是线性的，是一条直线。

sentences.en: It was not linear. I had really fast improvement at the beginning, but then I hit a learning plateau.
sentences.zh: 它并不是线性的。我在刚开始时进步神速，但随后我遭遇了学习平台期。

sentences.en: A learning plateau is when your progress stops.
sentences.zh: 学习平台期就是指你的进步停滞不前的时期。

sentences.en: Perhaps even language ability deteriorates.
sentences.zh: 甚至语言能力可能还会倒退。

sentences.en: You become worse at the language. There are many reasons why progress would not be linear.
sentences.zh: 你的语言变差了。进步不是线性的原因有很多。

sentences.en: People’s motivation changes. Mine certainly did.
sentences.zh: 人们的动力会发生变化。我的当然也变了。

sentences.en: Life changes. I moved from living in Japan back to the UK in 2018 and that was certainly a reason for not studying Japanese as much.
sentences.zh: 生活在变。我在2018年从日本搬回了英国，这绝对是我没法像以前那样大量学日语的原因之一。

sentences.en: Now I have much less time, which means I can’t dedicate hours a day to studying Japanese like I used to when I was in my early 20s.
sentences.zh: 现在我的时间少多了，这意味着我无法像20出头时那样每天花几个小时专门学日语了。

sentences.en: So language learning is not a straight line.
sentences.zh: 所以语言学习绝不是一条直线。

sentences.en: Progress is not guaranteed. The second thing I regret is losing structure.
sentences.zh: 进步并不是打包票的。我后悔的第二件事是失去了规律性。

sentences.en: When I first studied Japanese, I was really structured in my progress.
sentences.zh: 刚开始学日语时，我的学习非常有条理。

sentences.en: I took three classes a week. I would study for at least one hour a day, usually after work, but sometimes before work as well.
sentences.zh: 我一周上三次课。我每天至少学习一个小时，通常在下班后，但有时上班前也会学。

sentences.en: I used textbooks consistently. I knew I had classes.
sentences.zh: 我一直坚持使用教科书。我知道自己有课要上。

sentences.en: I knew I had study time. I knew I was going to use textbooks.
sentences.zh: 我知道自己有学习时间。我知道自己会用到课本。

sentences.en: But I have lost that structure now. I don’t use the textbook correctly.
sentences.zh: 但现在我失去了这种规律。我没有正确使用课本。

sentences.en: I don’t take classes enough. I don’t study daily.
sentences.zh: 我上课不够频繁。我不再每天学习。

sentences.en: If I have free time now, it’s either spent working or with my family.
sentences.zh: 如果现在我有空闲时间，要么用来工作，要么陪家人。

sentences.en: That’s kind of it. Life is busy. Once you hit that intermediate level of a language, it’s easy to stop your structure.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是这样。生活很忙碌。一旦你达到了语言的中级水平，就很容易打破原有的规律。

sentences.en: It’s easy to drift away from what had been helping you work.
sentences.zh: 你很容易偏离那些曾经帮助你不断进步的方法。

sentences.en: I had made great progress with having a organized day of studying, and just as I was reaching the peak of my Japanese progress, I moved to the UK.
sentences.zh: 我原本通过井井有条的每日学习取得了巨大的进步，而就在我达到日语巅峰状态的时候，我搬回了英国。

sentences.en: And I stopped studying every day, and I stopped taking Japanese classes for a few months, and I stopped speaking in Japanese regularly.
sentences.zh: 我停止了每天的学习，好几个月没上日语课，也停止了经常说日语。

sentences.en: The third thing I regret from my studying experience is not practicing writing.
sentences.zh: 我在学习经历中后悔的第三件事是没有练习写作。

sentences.en: I think this is something that many of you listening probably can relate to.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是许多正在收听节目的朋友能够感同身受的一点。

sentences.en: I did not practice writing Japanese really at all for the first two years of studying the language.
sentences.zh: 在学习这门语言的前两年，我几乎完全没有练习过写日语。

sentences.en: I did write, I did learn how to write the Japanese characters, some of them, but I just didn’t really practice writing, handwriting especially.
sentences.zh: 我确实写过，我也学过怎么写日语汉字，其中的一部分，但我真的没有练习写作，尤其是手写。

sentences.en: An interesting story is that most of my Japanese writing ability developed after I studied Chinese instead.
sentences.zh: 一个有趣的的故事是，我的大部分日语书写能力其实是在我转头去学中文之后才培养出来的。

sentences.en: I started to study Chinese in 2018 when I was doing my master’s degree.
sentences.zh: 我在2018年读硕士学位时开始学中文。

sentences.en: I did Japanese as well, but I started to study Chinese, and as part of my Chinese classes at university, I had to write.
sentences.zh: 我也学了日语，但我开始学中文，作为大学中文课的一部分，我必须进行写作。

sentences.en: Chinese and Japanese partly share an alphabet.
sentences.zh: 中文和日语在某种程度上共用了一套字母系统。

sentences.en: The Japanese kanji alphabet is based off the Chinese alphabet, at least the historic version of it.
sentences.zh: 日语的汉字字母是基于汉字演变而来的，至少历史版本是这样的。

sentences.en: I assumed, when I first moved to Japan, that I wasn’t going to live here long term, and my focus was purely communication-based.
sentences.zh: 刚搬到日本时，我以为自己不会在这里长期居住，我的重点纯粹基于交流。

sentences.en: I wanted to be able to listen to people and reply to them.
sentences.zh: 我希望能听懂别人的话并做出回应。

sentences.en: I wanted to be able to have conversations.
sentences.zh: 我希望能够进行对话。

sentences.en: So I focused extensively on speaking and listening.
sentences.zh: 所以我把大量的精力集中在听说上。

sentences.en: I then did a little bit of reading practice as well, and gradually my reading improved, especially when it came to studying for language proficiency tests.
sentences.zh: 后来我也做了一点阅读练习，慢慢地我的阅读能力有所提高，特别是在备考语言能力测试的时候。

sentences.en: But the Japanese Language Proficiency Test does not require handwriting.
sentences.zh: 但是日语能力测试并不要求手写。

sentences.en: So now my Japanese writing ability is far lower than it should be.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我的日语书写能力远低于它应有的水平。

sentences.en: I have to do paperwork occasionally, and either I need to rely on my wife to help me write in Japanese, or I have to copy the Japanese characters across.
sentences.zh: 我偶尔需要处理一些公文，要么我得靠妻子帮我用日语写，要么我就得把日语汉字临摹下来。

sentences.en: For example, in January when I had to register the birth of my child and I needed to open up my phone, type out the characters so that I could write down the information I needed to write, because I couldn’t remember how to write the specific letters in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 例如，今年一月份我不得不去给我的孩子登记出生证明，我得打开手机，打出那些汉字，才能写下我需要填写的资料，因为我想不起来具体该怎么手写那些日语假名了。

sentences.en: This is perhaps a Japanese-specific issue in that the letters are difficult to write.
sentences.zh: 这或许是日语特有的问题，因为这些字很难写。

sentences.en: You have to remember thousands of different letters.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住几千个不同的字。

sentences.en: English doesn’t necessarily have that problem.
sentences.zh: 英语则没有这种烦恼。

sentences.en: But also, I never really practiced writing structured sentences in Japanese either.
sentences.zh: 而且，我也从未真正在日语中练习过写结构完整的句子。

sentences.en: I think if I had practiced writing more, I would be a better reader as well.
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果我多练习写作的话，我的阅读能力也会变得更好。

sentences.en: So I really encourage all of you guys to not neglect your writing.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的鼓励大家千万不要荒废了写作。

sentences.en: I encourage all of you to practice writing in English, because I never practiced writing in Japanese and now I really regret it.
sentences.zh: 我鼓励所有人多练习英语写作，因为我当年没练日语写作，现在肠子都悔青了。

sentences.en: A fourth regret I have is spending money on the wrong resources.
sentences.zh: 我第四个后悔的事情是把钱花在了错误的学习资料上。

sentences.en: I have spent a lot of money studying Japanese, maybe not as much as some of you guys have spent learning English.
sentences.zh: 我在学日语上花了很多钱，也许不像你们有些人学英语花得那么多。

sentences.en: One thing I like to do is buy textbooks.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢做的一件事就是买教科书。

sentences.en: I think on my desk right now I currently have five Japanese textbooks that I barely use.
sentences.zh: 我想我现在的桌上目前放着五本我几乎不怎么翻的日语教材。

sentences.en: In fact, a few of them I’ve never used. Textbooks are something that, because they were so effective in my first few years of studying Japanese, I rely on a lot.
sentences.zh: 事实上，其中有几本我从来没用过。因为教科书在我学日语的前几年非常有效，所以我非常依赖它们。

sentences.en: But I struggle to find time to complete the exercises.
sentences.zh: 但我却很难抽出时间来做完上面的练习题。

sentences.en: I end up buying a lot of textbooks with the hope they’re going to motivate me, and then not really using them.
sentences.zh: 我结果买了一大堆教材，希望它们能激励我，然后却并不怎么用它们。

sentences.en: I’ve also taken courses before, classes online that I just didn’t enjoy.
sentences.zh: 我还曾经报过一些我根本不喜欢的在线课程。

sentences.en: They were a waste of time really. And I bought resources because they seemed useful rather than actually worth the money.
sentences.zh: 那真的完全是在浪费时间。我买这些资源是因为它们看起来很有用，而不是它们真的物有所值。

sentences.en: In fact, I had a Japanese learning app on my phone for 3 years, paying £10 a month that I forgot I had.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我的手机上曾有一个日语学习软件挂了3年，每个月扣我10英镑，我都忘了自己还订购了它。

sentences.en: My fifth regret is that I didn’t take advantage of every opportunity I have been offered over the past 10 years.
sentences.zh: 我第五个后悔的事，是没有抓住过去10年中提供给我的每一个机会。

sentences.en: By opportunity, I mean the chance to use Japanese or the opportunity to develop my skills.
sentences.zh: 这里所说的机会，指的是使用日语的机会或是提升自己技能的机会。

sentences.en: Let me give you a few examples. I live in Japan now.
sentences.zh: 我举几个例子。我现在住在日本。

sentences.en: I’ve lived here seven out of the past ten years, and I’ve lived here for the past three years non-stop.
sentences.zh: 在过去的10年里有7年我住在这里，而且过去3年我是一直呆在这里没中断过。

sentences.en: Likely I’ll live here for a long time. I don’t use as much Japanese as I should.
sentences.zh: 我大概率会在这里住很长时间。但我用的日语其实并不算多。

sentences.en: I don’t use business Japanese. I don’t watch much Japanese media.
sentences.zh: 我不用商务日语。我不怎么看日本媒体。

sentences.en: I don’t read many Japanese books. I could immerse myself in Japanese far more than I currently do, but I don’t really.
sentences.zh: 我不怎么看日本书。我本可以让自己更多地沉浸在日语环境里，但我并没有这么做。

sentences.en: I am not taking advantage of the opportunities I have.
sentences.zh: 我没有充分利用我拥有的这些机会。

sentences.en: I probably should immerse myself more. When I first moved to the island of Shikoku, I did take every opportunity.
sentences.zh: 我可能应该让自己更多地沉浸进去。刚搬到四国岛时，我确实抓住了每一个机会。

sentences.en: But when I moved to Tokyo in COVID, for the first year, I didn’t really take any opportunities to study Japanese.
sentences.zh: 但在疫情期间搬到东京后，第一年里，我其实并没有抓住任何学日语的机会。

sentences.en: I was a research student at a university in Tokyo, and I had the opportunity to take free Japanese classes, but I didn’t for the the first term.
sentences.zh: 我是东京一所大学的研究生，我本有机会免费上日语课，但在第一个学期我却没去上。

sentences.en: I don’t know why. I just didn’t take those Japanese classes.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么。我就是没去上那些日语课。

sentences.en: I think this is important for all of you listening.
sentences.zh: 我想这对所有收听节目的朋友都很重要。

sentences.en: Make use of all the opportunities you have to learn English.
sentences.zh: 充分利用你拥有的所有学习英语的机会。

sentences.en: Take the opportunity to practice and you never know what benefits you will get from that practice opportunity.
sentences.zh: 抓住机会去练习，你永远不知道这种练习机会会带给你什么样的好处。

sentences.en: After 10 years of studying Japanese, the biggest lesson that I’ve learned is that language learning is part of my life now.
sentences.zh: 学了10年日语之后，我学到的最大教训是：语言学习现在已经成为了我生活的一部分。

sentences.en: It’s not a project I’m trying to finish.
sentences.zh: 它不是一个我正试图完成的项目。

sentences.en: Language learning is part of my identity.
sentences.zh: 语言学习是我身份的一部分。

sentences.en: I started learning Japanese for survival, for necessity.
sentences.zh: 我开始学日语是为了生存，是为了必需。

sentences.en: Then my motivation was passing exams or making friends.
sentences.zh: 后来我的动力变成了通过考试或交朋友。

sentences.en: Now it’s about continuing to improve so I can fully participate in the life I’m building here in Japan.
sentences.zh: 现在则是为了不断提高，以便能够全面参与到我在这里建立的生活中去。

sentences.en: I’m not a perfect Japanese speaker, and I’m definitely not finished in my learning journey, and I never will be finished.
sentences.zh: 我不是一个完美的日语说话者，我的学习之旅也绝对没有结束，而且永远也不会结束。

sentences.en: After 10 years, I’m still learning and I’m proud of that.
sentences.zh: 10年过去了，我仍在学习，我为此感到骄傲。

sentences.en: I am a language learner. I am a Japanese learner.
sentences.zh: 我是一个语言学习者。我是一个日语学习者。

sentences.en: And I don’t think I will ever stop learning.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我永远不会停止学习。

sentences.en: There’ll still be new things to learn. There’ll still be new opportunities to take.
sentences.zh: 依然会有新东西要学。依然会有新机会去把握。

sentences.en: And so that’s my biggest lesson, is that you shouldn’t think of learning English as something that you will complete.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我最大的教训，那就是你千万不要把学英语当成一件有终点的事。

sentences.en: It’s not a task for you to do. It is something that will be with you for as long as you want it to be, perhaps for all of your life.
sentences.zh: 它不是一项要你打勾完成的任务。只要你愿意，它会一直伴随着你，也许会伴随你的一生。

sentences.en: And you will improve, and you will hit plateaus.
sentences.zh: 你会进步，你也遭遇瓶颈。

sentences.en: Maybe you’ll lose some of your confidence, then you’ll improve again, and it’s something that is part of your life.
sentences.zh: 也许你会失去一些信心，然后你又会再次进步，它是你生活不可分割的一部分。

sentences.en: But what do you think? How long have you been studying English?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看呢？你学英语多久了？

sentences.en: What are your proudest accomplishments, and what are your biggest regrets?
sentences.zh: 你最自豪的成就是什么，你最大的遗憾又是什么？
